title: Drumming on the pot
hook: at his wife's death Zhuangzi is found singing, and explains that he grieved, then saw the seasons turning (Zhuangzi 18)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Huizi, Zhuangzi's friend on the bridge, and the joy of fish. Your line was I know it from the bridge.

This one is about grief, so let's go gently. If you're carrying a fresh loss right now, you're welcome here exactly as you are; nothing in this story asks you to feel any particular way. Zhuangzi's wife has died, after many years together. His old friend Huizi, the one from the bridge, comes to the house to pay his respects. And he finds Zhuangzi sitting on the ground, legs sprawled out, banging on a clay pot like a drum, and singing.
screen: `A STORY ABOUT GRIEF.` → `HUIZI COMES TO MOURN.` → `ZHUANGZI IS SINGING.`

segments.voice: Huizi is shocked. She lived with you, he says. She raised your children. She grew old with you. It would be enough not to weep for her. But drumming on a pot and singing? Isn't that going too far? Zhuangzi's answer starts with grief. When she first died, do you think I didn't grieve? Of course I did. The story says so plainly. But then, he says, I looked back to her beginning. Before she was born, there was no life. Before that, no body. Before that, not even breath. Then, somewhere in the great mystery of things, there was a change, and there was breath. The breath changed, and there was a body. The body changed, and there was life. Now there's been another change, and she has died. It's like the turning of the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter. She's lying at rest now, in the great room of the world. If I followed her crying and wailing, it would show I didn't understand how things go. So I stopped. Different traditions, and different families, grieve in very different ways, and this story doesn't rank any of them. It's not a rule against crying. Zhuangzi cried. It's what he found on the far side of crying: his wife's life as part of something larger, still moving, like a year. Winter isn't the year going wrong. It's the year. And the pot and the song were what he had left to give her.
screen: `ISN'T THAT GOING TOO FAR?` · `DO YOU THINK I DIDN'T GRIEVE?` · `BREATH, BODY, LIFE, CHANGE.` · `LIKE THE FOUR SEASONS.` · then, large: `SEASONS TURN.`

segments.voice: Sit with one loss as a season: it can be small, a place you moved from, a friendship that faded, a pet, and if a big loss is too near, choose a small one, or simply breathe. Remember its spring, its summer, its autumn, and let it be winter now, without forcing anything. If tears come, let them; Zhuangzi had his too. And if a loss ever feels too heavy to carry alone, reach out: in the US you can call or text 988 at any hour, and elsewhere, local emergency help.
four seasons, spring, summer, autumn, winter. Zhuangzi grieved his wife, then sang, seeing her life as one more turning of them.
Your line: seasons turn. Zhuangzi grieved first, and then he sang. Go gently; see you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Taoist readers take Zhuangzi's drumming as a teaching about accepting death as part of the transformation of all things; readers from traditions that mourn in very different ways read it too, as one man's path through grief rather than a rule.
